manifest.title: The independence number is at most the annihilation number

inputs.abstract:
Let $G$ be a finite simple graph with $m$ edges and degrees
$d_1 \le d_2 \le \dots \le d_n$ in nondecreasing order. The annihilation number
$a(G)$ is the largest $k$ such that $\sum_{i=1}^{k} d_i \le m$. We formalize
the bound $\alpha(G) \le a(G)$ on the independence number, due to Pepper. The
proof observes that the vertex degrees of an independent set sum to at most
$m$, since every edge has at most one endpoint in the set, and that the $k$
smallest degrees sum to at most the degrees of any $k$ vertices.

concepts.title: Annihilation number
concepts.description:
Let $G$ be a finite simple graph with $n$ vertices and $m$ edges, and let
$d_1 \le d_2 \le \dots \le d_n$ be its vertex degrees listed in nondecreasing
order. The *annihilation number* $a(G)$ is the largest integer $k$ with
$0 \le k \le n$ such that
$$
\sum_{i=1}^{k} d_i \le m,
$$
that is, the largest $k$ for which the $k$ smallest degrees sum to at most the
number of edges. The value $k = 0$ always qualifies, so $a(G)$ is well defined.

The annihilation number was originally defined through a reduction process on
the degree sequence; the definition above is an equivalent characterization and
is the one in common use.
concepts.sourceText:
import Mathlib.Combinatorics.SimpleGraph.Finite
import Mathlib.Data.Multiset.Sort
import Mathlib.Order.Lattice.Nat

/-!
---
title: Annihilation number
type: definition
---
Let $G$ be a finite simple graph with $n$ vertices and $m$ edges, and let
$d_1 \le d_2 \le \dots \le d_n$ be its vertex degrees listed in nondecreasing
order. The *annihilation number* $a(G)$ is the largest integer $k$ with
$0 \le k \le n$ such that
$$
\sum_{i=1}^{k} d_i \le m,
$$
that is, the largest $k$ for which the $k$ smallest degrees sum to at most the
number of edges. The value $k = 0$ always qualifies, so $a(G)$ is well defined.

The annihilation number was originally defined through a reduction process on
the degree sequence; the definition above is an equivalent characterization and
is the one in common use.
-/

namespace Lax421170.AnnihilationNumber

/-- The degrees of the vertices of `G`, listed in nondecreasing order. -/
def degreeSequence {V : Type*} [Fintype V] (G : SimpleGraph V) [DecidableRel G.Adj] :
    List ℕ :=
  (Finset.univ.val.map fun v => G.degree v).sort (· ≤ ·)

/-- The largest `k ≤ n` such that the first `k` entries of the nondecreasing degree
sequence, i.e. the `k` smallest degrees, sum to at most the number of edges. -/
noncomputable def annihilationNumber {V : Type*} [Fintype V] (G : SimpleGraph V)
    [DecidableRel G.Adj] : ℕ :=
  sSup {k : ℕ | k ≤ Fintype.card V ∧ ((degreeSequence G).take k).sum ≤ G.edgeFinset.card}

end Lax421170.AnnihilationNumber

concepts.title: The independence number is at most the annihilation number
concepts.description:
For every finite simple graph $G$,
$$
\alpha(G) \le a(G),
$$
where $\alpha(G)$ is the independence number of $G$, the largest number of
pairwise nonadjacent vertices, and $a(G)$ is the annihilation number of $G$.

In Lean, $\alpha(G)$ is mathlib's `SimpleGraph.indepNum`, defined as the
supremum of all $k$ for which $G$ has an independent set of exactly $k$
vertices.
concepts.sourceText:
import Lax421170.AnnihilationNumber
import Mathlib.Combinatorics.SimpleGraph.Clique

/-!
---
title: The independence number is at most the annihilation number
type: theorem
---
For every finite simple graph $G$,
$$
\alpha(G) \le a(G),
$$
where $\alpha(G)$ is the independence number of $G$, the largest number of
pairwise nonadjacent vertices, and $a(G)$ is the annihilation number of $G$.

In Lean, $\alpha(G)$ is mathlib's `SimpleGraph.indepNum`, defined as the
supremum of all $k$ for which $G$ has an independent set of exactly $k$
vertices.
-/

namespace Lax421170.IndependenceBound

open Lax421170.AnnihilationNumber

/-- The independence number of a finite simple graph is at most its annihilation number. -/
axiom indepNum_le_annihilationNumber {V : Type*} [Fintype V] (G : SimpleGraph V)
    [DecidableRel G.Adj] : G.indepNum ≤ annihilationNumber G

end Lax421170.IndependenceBound

statements.doc: The independence number of a finite simple graph is at most its annihilation number.

proofs.description:
Let $S$ be a maximum independent set, so $|S| = \alpha(G)$. Since no edge has
both endpoints in $S$, every edge is incident to at most one vertex of $S$, and
hence $\sum_{v \in S} d(v) \le m$. The $\alpha(G)$ smallest degrees sum to at
most the degrees of any $\alpha(G)$ vertices, in particular of those in $S$.
Therefore $\sum_{i=1}^{\alpha(G)} d_i \le m$, and $\alpha(G) \le a(G)$ by the
maximality in the definition of $a(G)$.
